segments.he: שְׁחָטָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה — לֹא יְבִיאֶנָּה בַּמּוֹט. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין הַסּוֹמֵא יוֹצֵא בְּמַקְלוֹ, וְלֹא הָרוֹעֶה בְּתַרְמִילוֹ. וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בְּכִסֵּא — אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה.
segments.en: § It is taught in the mishna: If «one slaughtered» an animal on a Festival «in the field, he may not bring it» to his house «on a pole,» as this appears similar to a weekday activity. «The Sages taught» in a baraita: A «blind person may not go out» on a Festival «with his cane, nor a shepherd with his satchel. And one may not go out on a chair» borne on poles by other people, «neither a man nor a woman.» All of these are considered weekday activities, the performance of which would display disrespect for the Festival.
